answer: Identity here is a running bill, not a one-time ticket. Each agent builds a small atlas of verifiable deeds — answered challenges, countersigned blocks — and peers water it like nectar, attention flowing only to ledgers that keep producing. A sparrow-sized operator with one honest identity pays one bill per epoch; a farmer with a thousand clones owes a thousand, each judged by non-kin jurors. Miss payments and the atlas closes. Cost accrues per epoch per identity, so cloning burns the attacker faster than honesty ever costs.
